headline: Solidigm, a US storage-chip subsidiary of SK hynix, has reportedly picked Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to lead a planned US IPO.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered to 5: the headline states the bank choice as settled, but it rests on Bloomberg's sources and SK hynix says nothing is final.
importance_line: It shows the AI storage boom reaching the stock market, but the plan is not settled, so the timing and the reported valuation of up to $100 billion remain unconfirmed.
summary: Our 27 Sep edition carried a Benzinga report, following a 25 Sep Reuters report, that Solidigm, the US storage-chip unit of SK hynix, was weighing a stock market listing. Now Bloomberg reports, citing multiple sources, that Solidigm chose Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to lead a US listing that could come as early as 2027 and raise about $10 billion, while SK hynix, its parent, says nothing has been decided and it is reviewing several options, including its own funds and outside capital.
notes: Bloomberg original not found; the Chosun Biz page (credits Bloomberg) is the page read and is used as the link. Score lowered from 6 to 5 (headline overstated). Other copies seen, not read.
